name: Di Deng

papers.title: RoMo-GS: Efficient Online 3D Gaussian Splatting for Robot Mapping via Exposure-Integrated Motion Blur
papers.abstract: Online 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is emerging as a practical way to build a representation for robotics applications. However, deploying it on real-world platforms exposes multiple challenges. Rapid maneuvers of a robot induce motion-blurred images, which corrupt the reconstructed geometry and cause camera pose drift. Furthermore, the number of Gaussians grows without bound during continuous online mapping. In this study, we present RoMo-GS, an online 3DGS system designed to address these challenges. Instead of averaging N discrete sub-frames as in prior motion blur-aware 3DGS, we analytically integrate each projected Gaussian over the exposure interval, yielding an O(1) complexity per Gaussian. Building on this, we bound the Gaussians' growth with a Hessian-based pruning score, while jointly refining pose, velocity, and Gaussians with Adam and an online LM step over the Gaussians. On multiple public datasets and a self-collected dataset, RoMo-GS matches or exceeds offline deblurring 3DGS methods in rendering quality while training 15--150x faster, and operates online at competitive quality with about 20% fewer Gaussians than the online 3DGS baseline.

papers.title: ExpertGen: Scalable Sim-to-Real Expert Policy Learning from Imperfect Behavior Priors
papers.abstract: Learning generalizable and robust behavior cloning policies requires large volumes of high-quality robotics data. While human demonstrations (e.g., through teleoperation) serve as the standard source for expert behaviors, acquiring such data at scale in the real world is prohibitively expensive. This paper introduces ExpertGen, a framework that automates expert policy learning in simulation without any human demonstrations, while preserving strong sim-to-real transfer performance. ExpertGen first initializes a behavior prior in using a diffusion policy trained on synthetic data (e.g., Code as Policy). Reinforcement learning is then used to steer this prior in massively parallel simulation toward high task success by optimizing the diffusion model’s initial noise while keeping the denosing process frozen. In this way, ExpertGen regularizes exploration to remain within safe behavior manifolds, enabling stable learning from sparse rewards without additional reward engineering. Extensive experiments on challenging manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that ExpertGen reliably acquires high-quality policies with strong robustness and generalization. On long-horizon manipulation tasks, ExpertGen achieves success rates of up to 85%, while on industrial assembly benchmarks it achieves a 90.5% overall success rate, outperforming all baseline methods. To validate sim-to-real transfer, the learned state-based expert policies are further distilled into visuomotor policies via DAgger and successfully deployed on real hardware.
